findings.title: Cascade: _nodb_cursor fallback registers 'default' pool on non-test DB
findings.why_it_matters: If 'postgres' is unreachable (the managed-hosting case the fallback exists for), the test run migrates, runs tests and flushes the real configured database instead of test_<NAME>. TransactionTestCase truncates its tables, so the data is lost. The fallback builds a wrapper with alias=self.alias ('default'), the real NAME and the inherited OPTIONS['pool']. Its first cursor creates and opens the class-level pool for 'default' with dbname=<real NAME>. conn.close() only returns the connection, so the pool stays registered. create_test_db then sets settings_dict['NAME'] to the test name, but the pool property only builds a pool when the alias is missing, so migrate and every test connection reuse the pool aimed at the real DB. In _clone_test_db the same fallback re-registers a pool on the template DB right after close_pool(); its background min_size connections can make CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE fail with 'source database is being accessed by other users'.

findings.title: assume_role with pool: configure callback re-enters the wrapper from a pool thread
findings.why_it_matters: With OPTIONS {'pool': ..., 'assume_role': ...} no pooled connection can be created, so every request hangs for the pool timeout (30s by default) and then fails with PoolTimeout. psycopg_pool runs the configure callback in its own worker threads. ensure_role calls ops.compose_sql(), which goes through mogrify(sql, params, self.connection), i.e. the Django wrapper that created the pool. If that wrapper is connected, validate_thread_sharing raises DatabaseError. If it is not connected, the worker calls wrapper.connect(), which calls pool.getconn() from inside the pool's own worker and deadlocks. The pool treats any Exception as a connection failure and keeps retrying with backoff. This breaks the in-code rule 'does not access anything on self aside from variables'. Building the statement from the raw psycopg connection removes the dependency on the wrapper and its thread.

findings.title: Alias-keyed pool survives create_test_db NAME switch
findings.why_it_matters: If anything opens the pooled alias before the test runner creates the test database (an AppConfig.ready() query, or a query at import time in a module the test suite imports), the per-alias pool is built with the real database's connection kwargs. create_test_db() then closes the connection and rewrites settings_dict['NAME'], but the pool is still in the class-level _connection_pools dict, so every later connect, including migrate, serialization, the tests themselves and TransactionTestCase flushes, goes back to the original (possibly production) database. Without a pool, close() plus the NAME rewrite was enough to retarget the alias. The diff already closes the pool for the same reason in _clone_test_db, _destroy_test_db and ensure_timezone, but not on the create path, the mirror path or setup_worker_connection.

findings.suggested_fix: Return orphaned connections to the pool. In get_new_connection(), after self.pool.getconn(), register weakref.finalize(self, connection._pool.putconn, connection) and keep the finalizer on the wrapper; call finalizer.detach() in _close() before the explicit putconn. Also add a note to the 'Connection pool' docs section that connections opened outside the request cycle must be closed (connections.close_all()) or they keep a pool slot. Assumption: putconn is thread-safe from a finalizer (psycopg_pool takes its own lock).
findings.title: Threads exiting without close() permanently leak pool slots
findings.why_it_matters: With pooling on, a borrowed connection only goes back to the pool when DatabaseWrapper._close() calls putconn. A worker thread (a threading.Thread, an executor job, a management-command helper) that uses the ORM and exits without connection.close() drops its thread-local wrapper, and the psycopg connection is garbage collected without any warning. psycopg_pool does not track checked-out connections and only decrements _nconns on putconn/close, so that slot is lost for good. With 'pool': True the defaults are min_size=4 and max_size=min_size, so four such threads are enough: after that every connection attempt in the process blocks for the 30 s pool timeout and then raises PoolTimeout. Before this change, the same leaked connection was simply closed when it was garbage collected.
source_keys: threads exiting without close() permanently leak pool slots

residual_risks: Session state leaks between pool borrowers: no reset callback is configured, so session-level state (SET search_path or other SET values, RESET/SET ROLE, temp tables, session advisory locks, LISTEN) survives close() and reaches the next borrower; before this change close() ended the session. A DISCARD ALL reset would also undo the configure-only SET ROLE/TIME ZONE, and _close() notes wrap_database_errors breaks with a reset function (reliability).

Connection or configure failures under pooling (database down, bad credentials, nonexistent assume_role) are only logged on the 'psycopg.pool' logger and retried in worker threads; each caller blocks in getconn() for the default 30 s timeout and gets an opaque PoolTimeout raised 'from None'. Consider documenting the 'timeout' pool option and the logger, or opening the pool with wait=True on first use (reliability, demoted from candidate #6).

OPTIONS['pool'] keys that collide with Django-supplied ConnectionPool arguments (kwargs, open, configure, check) raise TypeError 'got multiple values for keyword argument', although the docs describe the dict as passed to ConnectionPool; a user-supplied check or configure cannot be used (reliability candidate #10, adversarial).

Fork-mode parallel test workers inherit the class-level _connection_pools dict; setup_worker_connection() rewrites NAME and calls close() but not close_pool(), so if the parent holds a 'default' pool at fork time a worker would reuse a pool aimed at the main test DB with dead worker threads and shared sockets. Unconfirmed whether the parent reconnects after the last _clone_test_db (reliability, adversarial).

close_pool() reads self.pool (creating a pool if none exists) and does an unguarded del self._connection_pools[self.alias]; two concurrent close_pool() calls can raise KeyError, and a concurrent get_new_connection() can reopen the just-closed pool, leaving an unreferenced open pool. Only test and setting_changed paths call it (correctness, adversarial).

The pool's configure callback is bound to whichever wrapper instance first evaluated .pool and uses its cached timezone_name; update_connections_time_zone only clears cached properties on the current thread's wrappers, so a pool rebuilt from another thread after override_settings(TIME_ZONE=...) can carry a stale time zone (adversarial; test/settings-change path).

ConnectionPool(check=...) and ConnectionPool.check_connection require psycopg-pool 3.2; only tests/requirements/postgres.txt pins >=3.2.0 and the docs name no minimum, so an older psycopg-pool fails with TypeError rather than ImproperlyConfigured (adversarial; not verified against 3.1 offline).

The new base ensure_connection() atomic-block guard fires only when self.connection is None with in_atomic_block and closed_in_transaction set; built-in non-pooled backends keep self.connection non-None, but a third-party backend whose _close() sets self.connection = None now gets ProgrammingError instead of reconnecting (adversarial; callsite completeness: grep-only).
testing_gaps: No test combines OPTIONS['pool'] with OPTIONS['assume_role']; test_connect_role moved to no_pool_connection(), so the configure-callback SET ROLE path (finding #2) and a failing configure callback under pooling have no coverage (correctness, testing, reliability, adversarial).

No test builds a pool under one NAME and then exercises create_test_db / set_as_test_mirror / setup_worker_connection or the _nodb_cursor fallback with pooling enabled (findings #1, #3) (correctness, reliability, adversarial).
No test that a pooled connection borrowed in a thread that exits without close() is returned to the pool or that pool capacity is preserved (finding #4) (reliability).

test_connect_pool uses min_size=0 with a pool-wide timeout of 0.1 s, so the first two real connection setups (plus configure) must finish within 100 ms; on a slow CI host it can raise PoolTimeout spuriously. Pre-open the pool (min_size=2, open(wait=True, timeout=10)) so the short timeout governs only the exhausted-pool assertion (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:244, testing, demoted candidate #7).

The pool reset in ensure_timezone() and the connection._pool.putconn() return path are not exercised: test_connect_pool_with_timezone creates its pool inside the settings override, and its copied 'default_pool' wrapper is not in connections, so the setting_changed receiver never runs for it; the test would still pass if close_pool() were removed from ensure_timezone() (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:302, testing, demoted candidate #8).

test_cannot_open_new_connection_in_atomic_block sets in_atomic_block/closed_in_transaction by hand and never calls close() on a pooled connection, so nothing proves close() inside a transaction leaves connection None, raises on the next query, discards uncommitted work, and reconnects after the block (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:335, testing, demoted candidate #9).

Under pooling, features.django_test_skips disables the two behavioral health-check tests; the replacement only asserts psycopg_pool's private _check attribute and never exercises the close_if_health_check_failed() early return or a dead pooled connection being discarded (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:318, testing).

Untested branches: the psycopg_pool ImportError path (ImproperlyConfigured 'Error loading psycopg_pool module'), pool returning None for NO_DB_ALIAS, close_pool() in _clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db, and the new is_usable() connection-is-None early return (testing).

Coverage of the pooled path for base/transactions behavior depends on CI running the full suite with OPTIONS['pool']; the django_test_skips addition implies that run, but no such settings file is in the repo or diff. test_connect_pool_with_timezone also relies on USE_TZ=False in the runner settings (tests/test_sqlite.py sets it; a pooled CI settings file must too) (testing).

triage_groups.title: Pool identity across test-database NAME changes
triage_groups.context: The class-level pool is keyed only by alias and freezes connect kwargs at creation, so any pool that exists before a test-DB NAME rewrite keeps pointing at the original database.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Handle #1 first: strip OPTIONS['pool'] from the temporary wrapper in DatabaseWrapper._nodb_cursor's fallback (P0 data-loss path and the clone-template 'being accessed by other users' failure). Then apply #3: close the alias pool in PostgreSQL creation wherever NAME is rewritten (_create_test_db, set_as_test_mirror, setup_worker_connection), which also guards #1's data-loss mode from any other early pool creation.
triage_groups.why: Shared root cause (alias-only pool key surviving NAME changes) with complementary fixes in base.py and creation.py; both need the same NAME-switch regression test.
